chart_leg_findings: HYPOTHESIZE, and it is the one that was stated as numbers and lost them. H1 predicted '43 of the 45 berths carrying a moved address deposit cleanly afterwards, 2 still refuse'; the built path measured 45 carrying, 42 clean, 3 refusing. The third is survey-20260728T170650, held by a request-identity mismatch added 2026-08-03 that retro-reds a 2026-07-28 packet — a second, out-of-bounds mechanism, so the disposition worked on it and something else did not let go. THE CAUSE IS NAMEABLE: the pre-build sweep that produced 43/2 modelled judge_survey alone and never called the door's full shape record, so it was a count taken through a proxy for the thing being changed. The survey berth's own unknown had named that risk in advance and the hypothesis used the number anyway. Criteria 3 and 4 were restated as INVARIANTS at the verdict for exactly this reason, and that is the durable form: no berth is refused for a finding the successor order rescues, and every surviving refusal names an address that resolves to nothing.

CONSTRAIN, and this one did NOT bite — recorded because a bound that never bites is still evidence about the leg that wrote it. `out` carried 'the five sibling deposit paths — measured as not biting; widening them here is scope this ticket refused at cast'. Nothing in the build ever reached for them. A bound whose subject the build never approaches is cheap to write and tells the next voyage nothing about where the edge actually is; the bounds that earned their keep were the two naming judge_survey's flat rule and the forwarding doors, because the build wanted both.

SURVEY / the trouble store it read from. Criterion 6 had to be written against 'the three marks the door actually leaves today' — mode 0444, the ratified eight VALIDATION_FIELDS, and standing() recomputing the source fingerprint — because `trail_link`, the mark the standing trouble cairn-tester-validation-store-py-persist-validation... still names as 'the only hand that mints one', IS RETIRED. Measured: VALIDATION_FIELDS at cairn/devices/tester/device.py:68 carries eight fields and no trail_link, and cairn/devices/tester/validation_store.py:55 records that the chain retired with the append-only-ness it protected. The trouble's instrument therefore points at a mechanism that no longer exists, and it sits in the session-open inbox saying so every morning. Ticket owed: restate that trouble's instrument post-trail_link, or it can never be honestly cleared.

DECOMPOSE's `writes_to` at n=4, its first real use since it shipped: every one of the four build pieces named exactly one path and every one was right. The narrowness is the finding — the field takes a list, and nothing in this voyage tested it with more than one entry, so 'a piece names where its output lands' is proved for the single-file case only. AND IT CANNOT NAME COMMONS OUTPUT AT ALL: this voyage's actual products include a ticket amendment and a trouble disposition in CairnCommons, and there is no piece shape that can say so — writes_to is class-space-shaped, so the half of the work that lands in the other repo is invisible to the split that authored it.

the_score_is_the_count_and_the_count_is_.read_downward: AND THE BRACKET IS THE FINDING, not the number. 'validate -> verdict' scores the packet by how much you had to go looking behind it, and it can only do that when the build follows the packet. Here it read 6 — which would score this the thinnest-needed packet of the night, and the truth is the opposite: the looking all happened earlier and the packet was written knowing the answers. A score that inverts when the work is done out of order is measuring the ORDER, not the packet, and the observer being ticketed should count from the first call that touches the target code, not from the berth's stamp.

value.a: MEASURED AT CAST, and it is why this is not an n=1 annoyance: over 56 berthed survey packets, 45 are refused by the flat holdings-resolve judge and 43 of those are FULLY rescued by the forwarding order that already exists on the promotion side. The live bite today is n=2 — the two berths naming /home/akien/.cairn/inference/hosts.json, on tickets inference-domain-chat-verb and the-instance-address-is-resolved-never-spelled. The 43 are what the defect costs any re-deposit.

THE REASONING WAS RIGHT AND THE ENUMERATION WAS SHORT BY ONE. survey_holdings_resolve's docstring (2026-07-30) makes the asymmetry deliberate and states its condition exactly: 'only the promotion side, which alone stands downstream of a move, disposes'. The deposit meets that condition word for word and was simply not in view when there were two mouths and now there are three. Nothing here is a correction of a judgement; it is a census that was taken before the third caller existed.

MY FIRST READ OF THIS DEFECT WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED ON THE RECORD. I wrote 'the successor door exists and the judge never asks it' into the-instance-address-is-resolved-never-spelled's distinctions and pushed it. The promotion judge DOES ask it. The distinction there now carries the corrected version. Generalises: the second-cheapest measurement (read the judge's own source) was one grep away from the first, and the first one's story was more satisfying.

THE NUMBER I CARRIED THROUGH FIVE CHART STAGES WAS PRODUCED BY A MODEL OF THE MECHANISM, NOT BY THE MECHANISM — and it was wrong in the direction that flatters. 43-and-2 appears in the survey berth, in hypothesis 1, and in criteria 3 and 4. The built path says 42-and-3. The pre-build sweep composed judge_survey and _resolves_to by hand and never called the door's full shape record, so it could not see the third still-refused berth, which is held by a request-identity rule and not by a holdings lack at all. The survey berth's own unknown named this risk in advance and I berthed the number anyway. What the corpus corrected is not the build: it is the SHAPE of the claim. A snapshot criterion goes red at the moment its condition is satisfied, so both criteria were restated as invariants — no berth is refused for a finding the successor order rescues; every surviving holdings refusal names an address that resolves to nothing — and the counts are printed as evidence and asserted nowhere.

THE READING A COUNT CANNOT GIVE, and the probe would have been a healthy-looking corpse without it. Over a clean corpus this watch's two counts read 0 and 0 whether the disposition is wired or reverted — permanently, under a carrier that looks fine. That is the aider-shim class exactly (a measured half structurally dead beneath a green surface), and the ticket's own carrier clause called for it at cast, before there was a probe to be wrong. So the probe asks the wire BEHAVIORALLY: it borrows a berth the door accepts as it stands, points one holding at an address git records as moved, and reads three things — the berth door still refuses it, the deposit's gate does not, and deposit_survey reaches its NEXT check. Measured red under a reverted disposition while both counts stayed at zero. Generalises: when a watch reports an ABSENCE of failures, ask what distinguishes its zero from a dead instrument's zero, and build that reading too.

AND THE PROBE'S FIRST DRAFT READ THE WIRE BROKEN WHILE IT WAS FINE — the fixture trap, now wearing a probe's clothes. It picked its template berth by SHAPE (the first one carrying a constrain_ref) and got survey-20260728T170650, which the door refuses for a request-identity mismatch its chain has carried since 2026-08-03. So door_refuses read False for a reason that had nothing to do with the address under test. The template is chosen BY THE DOOR now — the first berth validate_survey ACCEPTS as it stands, newest first — so the moved address is the single lack introduced. Same lesson at a third seam: a fixture that agrees with the reader instead of the writer says nothing about the world.

A SIBLING DEFECT, NAMED AND NOT FIXED HERE: A DEPOSIT ALSO STANDS DOWNSTREAM OF A CHANGE TO THE RULES, not only to the world. survey-20260728T170650 is refused by a request-identity check added 2026-08-03 that retro-reds a 2026-07-28 packet; decompose-20260817T140525 is refused by decompose.writes_to, which grew a requirement after it berthed. Same shape as this ticket — a gate re-asked later, in a world that moved — but the thing that moved is the JUDGE, not the address, and no successor order can rescue it. Out of bounds here; owed a cast.

AND THE CLEARANCE GATE BIT ON THE WAY OUT, WHICH IS THE GATE DOING ITS JOB AND A POPULATION WORTH THE CENSUS. The PROVED crossing refused because survey's charter declared its owner in PROSE and prose cannot gate; one line, gated_by:['CC'], and it cleared. Census taken rather than the instance patched alone: 27 of 39 beside-code charters carry no gated_by — including four of the seven chart stages and verdict — so every one of them is a boat that cannot enter proven-space today, and will discover it at its own first PROVED crossing. Owed a cast.
